title: The Nothing Headphone (1) Pro Brought New Life to Music I’ve Listened to for Years
gist: Wired rates Nothing's $400 Headphone (1) Pro 9/10, praising a triple-driver design with an xMEMS tweeter, metal and glass construction and deep EQ customization, but noting ANC trails Sony and Bose. It is positioned $50 below the Sony XM6, Bose QC Ultra and AirPods Max 2.

insights.claim: Nothing's $400 Headphone (1) Pro is its first premium over-ear and competes with the $450 Sony WH-1000XM6, $450 Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd Gen) and the $550 (often $450) Apple AirPods Max 2, undercutting them.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: A challenger brand is attacking the premium ANC tier on price and design rather than ANC performance.

insights.claim: Wired rates the headphones 9/10 and says it is a toss-up whether the reviewer uses them or the Sony XM6 as a daily driver, which he calls high praise for Nothing's first premium over-ear.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Reviewers now view Nothing as credible against the incumbents, supporting its brand ascent.

insights.claim: Noise canceling and transparency are great but 'not quite as bulletproof as Sony and Bose', so the Nothing wins on design, tactile controls, sound profile and EQ rather than ANC.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: ANC leadership remains with Sony and Bose, which is the main moat for incumbents.

insights.claim: The Headphone (1) Pro uses aluminum cans, titanium arms and a glass outer window with little plastic yet weighs 2 grams less (327 g) than the Headphone (1), and is the most comfortable Nothing model.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Premium materials without a weight penalty support the step up in price tier.

insights.claim: The product uses a triple-driver design (bass dynamic, precision dynamic, treble xMEMS) while every other major ANC headphone brand uses a single dynamic driver, which the reviewer calls a big risk that paid off in sound quality.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: A MEMS tweeter in a consumer headphone is a signal for xMEMS adoption beyond earbuds.
insights.quote: When every other major ANC headphone brand uses a single dynamic driver for the full frequency range, this triple-driver design is a big risk.

insights.claim: EQ customization is unusually deep: a physical FLAT switch, a three-band simple EQ, an advanced mode with +/-6 dB per band on two drivers, five curated presets and spatial audio.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Software-tunable sound is a differentiator that is cheap to iterate for a challenger.

insights.claim: The tuning favors mids and treble over bass: it was less punchy than the Sony XM6 for Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar or EDM, and the reviewer found deep work focus harder than with bass-forward rivals.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Sound-signature trade-offs shape fit by user; EQ headroom mitigates it.

insights.claim: The hard-shell carry case, resembling the AirPods Max 2's near-universally loathed purse-like case, is a love-it-or-hate-it weak point.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Accessory design can drag on an otherwise strong hardware launch.

insights.claim: Key specs include Bluetooth 6.1 with Multipoint and Auracast, LDAC, 24-bit/192 kHz lossless over USB-C, IP52, and battery of up to 30 hours with ANC on or 68 hours with it off.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Spec parity with flagships at a lower price compresses incumbents' premium.
